Title: Sultan of Pahang, Tengku Ampuan extend condolences to Nizar
Article:
KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, and the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, have extended their condolences to Datuk Mohamad Nizar Najib on the death of his mother, Tengku Puteri Zainah Tengku Eskandar.
Nizar is the Pahang Investment, Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation Committee chairman.
Al-Sultan Abdullah and Tunku Azizah expressed sadness over the death and hoped that the entire family would be granted strength, fortitude, and patience in coping with the loss of their loved one.
"Their Royal Highnesses also pray that the soul of the deceased be blessed with the mercy of Allah, all sins forgiven, good deeds accepted, and that she be placed among the righteous and pious believers. Al-Fatihah," read a post on the Kesultanan Pahang Facebook page.
Meanwhile, Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail also conveyed his condolences to Nizar and his family in a Facebook post.
"May the entire family be granted strength, fortitude, and patience during this deeply sorrowful time," he said.
Tengku Puteri Zainah
died
at a hospital in the capital today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain expected in 8 states, Labuan till 10pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit several areas in eight states and Labuan till 10pm tonight.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said that the affected areas include Kubang Pasu, Baling, Sik and Padang Terap in Kedah; Lipis, Raub, Cameron Highlands and Rompin in Pahang, along with Larut Matang, Kampar, Kinta, Kuala Kangsar, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Hulu Perak, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Muallim, Batang Padang and Selama in Perak.
Other areas include Gua Musang in Kelantan, Hulu Selangor, Kuala Selangor, Gombak, Sabak Bernam and Klang in Selangor, as well as Kota Tinggi, Johor Baru and Mersing in Johor.
Finally, in Sarawak, the affected areas are Miri (Marudi, Telang Usan, Bario and Beluru) and Limbang, while in Sabah, Pensiangan, Sipitang, Beaufort, Kuala Penyu and Tenom in the Interior are affected.

Title: Police investigate elderly man's death as murder after viral abuse video
Article:
SEREMBAN: Police are investigating the death of an elderly man, who was allegedly beaten in Rasah Jaya here, as a murder case.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said police received a report about a viral TikTok video around 10am today.
"It showed a man in his 60s being abused by several people before he died yesterday evening," he said in a statement.
A video had earlier gone viral showing an elderly man in a wheelchair being beaten by two people, at a flat in Rasah Jaya.
Alzafny said police launched an investigation following the report and were probing the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
"A local man and two women, aged between 28 and 34, believed to be involved in the incident, have been arrested.
"Police also seized a rubber hose suspected to have been used to beat the victim, a wheelchair, a mobile phone and clothing," he said.
He assured that firm action would be taken against anyone involved, without compromise, and that a thorough investigation was underway in accordance with the law.
Earlier, a man from a non-governmental organisation (NGO) said he had come across the abuse video before visiting the location to investigate.
Upon arriving, he said a funeral was underway and he identified the deceased as the man seen being assaulted in the viral video.
The funeral was reportedly being conducted hastily, raising suspicions. It was stopped with police assistance, and the body was sent to hospital for a post-mortem examination.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Weststar helicopter project carries RM6.41bil price tag
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Weststar Aviation Sdn Bhd's helicopter supply and maintenance concession for the government carries an estimated project cost of RM6.41 billion.
MARC Ratings stated that this will be financed through a RM5.76 billion sukuk programme and RM640.5 million in shareholder equity.
MARC assigned a preliminary AA+IS rating with a stable outlook to Weststar Aviation's proposed sukuk of up to RM6 billion.
Under the 18-year concession administered by the National Security Council (MKN), Weststar Aviation will supply and maintain 28 helicopters for six government agencies involved in defence, security and emergency response operations.
The project also includes training for more than 1,440 pilots, crew members and engineers.
The helicopters will be deployed for utility missions, search and rescue operations, medical evacuations, security patrols and training.
MARC said the rating reflects strong and predictable cash flows from the government, the established operating track record of Weststar Aviation's parent Weststar Aviation Services Sdn Bhd (Weststar) and the manufacturing and delivery capabilities of helicopter maker Leonardo SpA.
However, these strengths are moderated by execution risks during the delivery phase, stringent aircraft availability requirements and potential delays in concession payments.
The sukuk will be issued progressively throughout the helicopter delivery period.
The first issuance of about RM3.83 billion, expected in 2026, will refinance existing syndicated facilities, partially reimburse eligible shareholder advances from the parent company and meet remaining initial project requirements.
Weststar will subsequently draw on a separate revolving credit facility to finance the remaining capital expenditure in 2027 through shareholder financing and advances to Weststar Aviation.
Subsequent sukuk issuances totalling about RM1.93 billion are expected in 2027 to refinance these advances.
Weststar has also committed additional shareholder support of up to 10 per cent of the total project cost to cover potential cost overruns, sukuk profit payments, fees and expenses.
MARC said debt servicing will be supported by fixed monthly concession payments for each helicopter, irrespective of flight-hour utilisation, subject to stipulated availability requirements.
Principal repayments are expected to begin in 2028 after all 28 helicopters are delivered, peaking at about RM515 million annually between 2031 and 2035.
The minimum and average finance service coverage ratios, including cash balances, are projected at 2.61 times and 3.59 times respectively between FY2028 and FY2039, comfortably above the minimum requirement of 1.65 times.
Execution risks are considered manageable, with all helicopters scheduled for delivery by December 2027, six months ahead of the concession deadline of June 2028.
The first helicopter for the Prime Minister's Department was delivered on Oct 15, 2026, followed by the first of two helicopters for the Fire and Rescue Department on Nov 1.
The second is scheduled for delivery in December, while the remaining 25 units are expected progressively throughout 2027.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RON95 contamination: Caltex, Petron drafting recovery programme for affected customers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two oil companies have begun drafting a customer recovery programme offering compensation to motorists whose vehicles suffered engine damage following complaints of contaminated RON95 petrol.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said Petron and Chevron, which operates the Caltex brand, were conducting the programme on a goodwill basis.
He said the move was initiated for verified complaints while investigations into the incidents continued.
"Caltex and Petron have drafted a customer recovery programme offering compensation on a goodwill basis based on established criteria, without any admission of wrongdoing or liability at this stage.
"Payments will be made to customers who have submitted complete complaints with valid supporting documents," he told the Dewan Rakyat during Ministers' Question Time.
He was responding to Abdul Latiff Abdul Rahman (PN-Kuala Krai), who sought the Chemistry Department's findings on RON95 samples collected from five states and oil depots, as well as measures to restore consumer confidence and compensate affected motorists.
On investigations, Armizan said preliminary analysis of 43 petrol samples by the Chemistry Department had found no evidence of water contamination.
He said an initial report dated Oct 29 showed water content below 0.05 per cent, the laboratory's minimum reportable detection limit.
"The remaining samples are still being analysed, and a full report will be issued once the department completes its tests.
"The immediate focus was on detecting water contamination, but none has been found so far. We are now examining the possible presence of other foreign substances and the fuel formulation during the period concerned," he said.
Armizan said 262 RON95 petrol samples had been collected from eight states and three oil company depots since complaints first emerged on Oct 3.
Both companies had also sent samples to their own laboratories, including those overseas, for further testing.
"Although the findings are not yet conclusive, the issue does not appear to affect the entire supply chain but rather fuel supplied during a specific period," he said.
Armizan stressed that the incidents were not being treated as isolated cases, despite being concentrated in certain locations and periods, particularly in Kedah and Penang.
He said some affected petrol stations remained closed.
To prevent similar incidents, the ministry was benchmarking Malaysia's fuel quality standards and supply chain monitoring practices against those of Singapore, the United Kingdom and Australia.
Armizan said motorists dissatisfied with the compensation offered could pursue other avenues, including lodging formal complaints with the ministry, filing civil suits or referring their cases to the Tribunal for Consumer Claims Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flash floods hit parts of Klang Valley after heavy rain
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Heavy rain this evening triggered flash floods in several parts of the Klang Valley, inundating roads in Setapak, Saujana Utama and Puncak Alam.
Social media users shared photographs and videos of the affected areas, with some warning motorists to avoid flooded roads.
In Setapak, floodwaters submerged part of Jalan Genting Klang in front of PV128 and a nearby petrol station.
Threads user @ieqaaiyaz shared photographs of the flooded stretch, advising motorists to avoid the area.
"The Setapak area, Jalan Genting Klang is badly flooded in front of PV128. Please be careful because the water is quite high.
"Avoid using this road if possible," she posted.
The post has since garnered more than 100,000 views.
In Saujana Utama, Sungai Buloh, an overflowing retention pond
triggered flash floods
in the area.
Facebook user Zamron Mat shared a video showing heavy rain in Taman Sri Alam, Saujana Utama, at 5.20pm in a community group for the area.
Threads user @afiqhhidayat also warned of rising water levels in nearby areas.
"Water has risen. Hillpark has flooded. Saujana Utama has flooded," he posted.
Meanwhile, Threads user @sophiloft shared a photograph of a flooded road and car park on the Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Puncak Alam campus.
The New Straits Times has contacted Kuala Lumpur City Hall, the Kuala Selangor Municipal Council and the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department for updates on emergency response and traffic management in the affected areas.
Fire stations across Selangor have also been instructed to
monitor flood-prone areas.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kobay profit jumps 73pct on revenue growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kobay Technology Bhd's net profit surged 73.3 per cent to RM18.65 million for the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27) from RM10.76 million in the corresponding quarter last year.
Its revenue rose 17.5 per cent to RM130.24 million from RM110.88 million in the previous corresponding quarter.
The engineering solutions provider said the stronger performance was primarily driven by its manufacturing division, which benefited from continued expansion in the semiconductor industry.
Its revenue from the manufacturing division increased 33.7 per cent year-on-year to RM96.3 million, accounting for 73.9 per cent of the group's total revenue.
Its pre-tax profit jumped 70.5 per cent to RM21 million from RM12.3 million a year earlier, supported by a higher sales mix of higher-margin products.
Kobay managing director and chief executive officer Datuk Seri Koay said the group recorded its highest quarterly net profit since its listing, surpassing the previous peak of RM15.1 million achieved in the third quarter of FY22.
He added that orders secured from the semiconductor industry had improved revenue visibility and were expected to support the group's performance in the coming months.
The group will also focus on improving capacity utilisation, operational efficiency and cost optimisation, while pursuing new customer opportunities and expanding its product and service offerings.
On a quarter-on-quarter basis, revenue remained relatively stable at RM130.2 million against RM131.8 million in the preceding quarter, while net profit increased 74 per cent from RM12.5 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police step up preparedness to face cyber threats
Article:
KULIM: Police are stepping up preparations to counter potential cyber threats linked to the escalating conflict between Iran and the United States, which could have implications for national security.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said developments in the conflict warranted serious attention, particularly the possibility of cyber threats emerging amid the volatile situation.
"We have indeed received information from overseas indicating that cyber threats are emerging amid the war between Iran and the United States.
"As such, we are continuously making preparations in the country. Instructions have also been issued to ensure that all matters concerning the issue of cyber threats are given greater attention," he said after launching Kedah police's 'Semarak Kebudayaan' programme at the KHTP Sports Complex today.
Meanwhile, he said the 'Semarak Masyarakat Bersama-sama PDRM' programme served as an important platform for bringing the police force closer to the community.
"This programme is very meaningful and important as it brings the police force closer to the community.
"There is a great deal of information that we can share to prevent crime and address other offences that require synergy between the community and police," he said.
He said that nearly 10,000 visitors were expected to attend the four-day programme, which began yesterday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flooding cuts off road to Puncak Alam for light vehicles
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Floodwaters about 0.6m deep rendered Jalan Meru Tambahan towards Puncak Alam impassable to light vehicles this evening.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received a distress call at 5.14pm.
He said seven firefighters from the Kapar Fire and Rescue Station were deployed and arrived at the scene about 10 minutes later.
"An inspection by the operation commander found that floodwaters had reached about two feet (0.6m), making the road impassable to light vehicles.
"However, no casualties were reported," he said in a statement.
Ashrul said the situation was brought under control at 5.40pm, with the operation ending at 6.09pm.
In a separate incident, Ashrul said the department received a report of flash flooding at Jalan Haji Supi, Kampung Salak, Sepang, at 5.37pm.
He said nine firefighters from the Sepang Fire and Rescue Station arrived at 5.59pm and found that the floodwaters had receded.
"Firefighters then monitored water levels in nearby areas to ensure the situation remained under control.
"The operation was reported to be under control at 6.10pm," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: PH victory can strengthen state-federal ties, says Anwar
Article:
MELAKA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on Melaka voters to give Pakatan Harapan candidates a mandate to ensure the state's development agenda can continue through cooperation with the federal government.
He said cooperation between the state and federal governments would facilitate the implementation of various development plans and ensure more benefits could be channelled to the people.
He said having elected representatives who worked with the federal government would make it easier to bring further development to the state.
"What matters in Melaka is that, even if we do not form the state government, opposition representatives should at least be able to speak up.
"If our candidates win, they will be able to work with me, making things much easier. We want to do better here, so give us your cooperation. That is all I am asking for," he said.
Anwar was speaking at the Jelajah Aspirasi Madani programme for the Klebang constituency at Taman Bukit Rambai here today.
He said several issues still required attention, including water and electricity supply, drainage systems and school toilet facilities.
He said the government should not focus solely on the country's economic achievements, but must also ensure that the people benefited from them, including through efforts to address the rising cost of living.
Anwar said he had consistently taken a grassroots approach, including visiting food stalls every Friday, to listen directly to the people's concerns.
"I do not want to be a politician who only shakes hands with villagers and visits food stalls when an election is near. I do this every Friday.
"If I do not, you can hold me accountable," he said.
Meanwhile, he said major investments in the country had also created job opportunities and helped enhance the skills of young people, including in technology and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).
He cited Google's RM61 billion investment, which he said had the potential to create about 30,000 job opportunities.
Anwar also stressed that the federal government had never sidelined states governed by the opposition, citing Kelantan, which continued to receive assistance during floods.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCMC testing internet coverage along ECRL route ahead of Dec 12 launch
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is conducting speed tests along the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) to identify areas that require improved internet coverage ahead of the service's launch on Dec 12.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the tests use the MCMC Nexus system and cover the route from Gombak to Kota Bharu, including its 16 stations and areas inside tunnels.
"MCMC is not only conducting internet speed tests along the journey from Gombak to Kota Bharu but also at the 16 ECRL stations.
"Through these tests, we can identify areas that remain 'greenfield', meaning no coverage at all, as well as 'brownfield' locations that have coverage but not yet sufficient, including inside tunnels, so that follow-up action can be taken," she said at a press conference at the Kuala Terengganu ECRL Station, during her working visit to Terengganu from today until tomorrow.
Also present were MCMC Eastern Region Office senior director Mohd Fairus Mohamad and Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak.
Teo sadi Maxis Bhd, which MRL appointed as the 4G mobile network infrastructure provider along the ECRL route, had presented its project implementation plan covering the provision of telecommunications infrastructure and network equipment upgrades.
She said the works were scheduled to begin after the site handover process from the construction contractor, China Communications Construction Company, to MRL is finalised tomorrow.
She added that expanding internet coverage would take time, and that MCMC would continue to work with service providers and MRL to address areas still experiencing connectivity problems.
Earlier, Teo, together with an MCMC delegation and Darwis, joined an ECRL train test run from the Gombak Integrated Terminal to the Kuala Terengganu ECRL Station, which took about three hours.
During the test run, she listened to an MCMC presentation on the results of internet speed tests conducted inside the train.
The 378km journey is part of the Phase 1 ECRL alignment, which connects Gombak to Kota Baru over 519km through 16 stations, ahead of the target for commercial operations in December.
The service linking the Klang Valley to the East Coast will use 11 Electric Multiple Unit train sets, each with a capacity of up to 425 passengers and a maximum speed of 160km per hour.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sentral Reit's profit inches up
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sentral Reit's net profit for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26) rose 0.7 per cent to RM19.82 million from RM19.69 million in the corresponding quarter last year.
Its revenue for the quarter increased 0.7 per cent to RM48.58 million from RM48.26 million previously.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, net profit grew 0.5 per cent to RM59.71 million from RM59.43 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 1.6 per cent to RM145.68 million from RM143.42 million.
Sentral Reit's manager Sentral Reit Management Sdn Bhd said the year-to-date performance was supported by higher portfolio occupancy, improved rental rates and higher finance income, which helped mitigate increased property operating expenses.
Its portfolio occupancy rate improved to 90 per cent as at Sept 30, 2026, compared with 86 per cent in the corresponding period last year, marking six consecutive quarters of improvement.
Of the 124,000 sq ft of net lettable area due for renewal in the first nine months of 2026, representing 5.8 per cent of its total net lettable area, 84 per cent of leases were successfully renewed.
Sentral Reit chairman Tan Sri Saw Choo Boon said crossing the 90 per cent occupancy mark reflected the appeal of its well-connected properties as tenants increasingly sought quality office space.
"Arcoris Mont' Kiara is contributing to revenue meaningfully, and recycling capital from Wisma Sentral Inai has strengthened Sentral REIT's balance sheet," he said.
He added that the REIT remained committed to building a more diversified and resilient portfolio.
As at Sept 30, 2026, Sentral Reit's total assets stood at RM2.6 billion, with its net asset value per unit improving to RM1.1169 from RM1.1144 as at Dec 31, 2025.
Chief executive officer Tay Hui Ling said the Reit was well positioned to pursue selective, accretive acquisitions to further diversify its portfolio and support sustainable growth in distributions to unitholders.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: WCE expects over 160,000 vehicles daily during Deepavali peak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than 160,000 vehicles a day are expected to use the West Coast Expressway (WCE) during the Deepavali peak as motorists travel home for the long weekend.
West Coast Expressway Sdn Bhd said the projected traffic volume was part of an estimated 3.28 million vehicles a day expected on major highways nationwide during the festive period.
In preparation for the increase, construction and maintenance works requiring lane closures will be suspended from Nov 6 to 10, except for urgent repairs and emergency works.
The company said patrol teams and the Emergency Response Team (ERT) would remain on standby round the clock, supported by tow trucks stationed along the expressway to assist motorists in the event of breakdowns or traffic incidents.
"Continuous traffic monitoring and response coordination will also be prioritised to minimise congestion and maintain smooth traffic flow throughout the expressway," it said.
West Coast Expressway Sdn Bhd managing director Lyndon Alfred Felix said cooperation and responsible driving among highway users were essential to ensuring safer journeys.
"Festive celebrations are a meaningful time for families and loved ones to come together. With higher traffic volumes anticipated on the roads, WCE remains committed to delivering efficient highway services while encouraging every motorist to play their part in ensuring the safety of all road users.
"Our operational teams are well prepared to manage the anticipated increase in traffic. However, road safety also depends on the attitude and actions of every driver.
"We therefore encourage motorists to plan their journeys ahead, remain alert to their surroundings and practise consideration towards fellow road users," he said.
Motorists can use the WCE App for real-time traffic updates, live closed-circuit television views and route guidance, as well as information on electric vehicle charging stations, motorcycle shelters and emergency telephones.
The Touch 'n Go PayDirect system is also available at all toll plazas along the expressway, allowing toll charges to be deducted directly from the eWallet balance linked to users' Touch 'n Go cards.
The expressway's six rest and service areas offer parking, prayer rooms and restrooms. Food stalls are available at the Sungai Nyior rest area in both directions and at the Bukit Kapar rest area northbound.
Motorists are advised to check their tyres, brakes and fluid levels before travelling, observe speed limits, ensure all passengers wear seat belts and use child restraint systems where applicable, and check their Touch 'n Go balances in advance. They are also reminded to take breaks when tired.
The company also welcomed the government's 50 per cent toll discount for eligible Class 1 vehicles on Nov 6 and 7.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi announced today that the discount would apply to Class 1 private vehicles at all toll plazas and Class 2 vehicles on the Penang Bridge, from 12.01am on Friday until 11.59pm on Saturday.
The discount excludes the border toll plazas at Bangunan Sultan Iskandar and Tanjung Kupang.
He said the government would bear an
estimated RM20.11 million in compensation
to highway concessionaires, with the initiative aimed at easing travel costs for Hindus returning to their hometowns or visiting family during Deepavali.
The 233km West Coast Expressway connects Banting in Selangor to Taiping in Perak.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Deepavali bazaars remain preferred choice despite online competition
Article:
SEREMBAN: The trend of online shopping is increasingly gaining the attention of consumers, but it does not overshadow physical bazaars as part of the Indian community still prefers to personally procure Deepavali necessities ahead of the Festival of Lights celebration this Sunday.
A Bernama survey at the Deepavali Carnival Bazaar in Jalan Dato Lee Fong Yee, also known as Little India Seremban, found that visitors are still flocking to the bazaar to obtain various festive necessities, including traditional clothing, snacks and home decorations.
Indian traditional clothing trader, N. Leena, 37, said customers still have the option to get festive clothing at the bazaar even though online shopping is gaining more attention.
She said the price of traditional clothing, which previously could reach RM250 to RM300, is now offered at around RM150 to RM180, thus providing more options for consumers.
"Many young people nowadays prefer to shop online, but there are still customers who choose to buy clothes at the bazaar in order to see, try, and assess the fabric material themselves here," she told Bernama.
Meanwhile, jewellery and prayer necessities trader, V. Preeya, 39, said her shop offers a variety of items with discounts of up to 50 per cent in conjunction with the carnival.
Preeya, who has been trading there for the past seven years, said that physical stores are still the choice of the Indian community, especially the elderly, even though online sales are gaining more attention.
"Every year we do business here by offering a variety of goods and special promotions. Although there is competition from online sales, older people still prefer to come to the store to shop," she said.
For henna hand artist, M. Bvithra, 30, the demand for henna painting services increases ahead of the Deepavali celebration as she receives double the usual bookings.
With a 12-year experience in the field, Bvithra said that customers, including the Malay community, also seek henna painting services at her shop, with prices starting from RM5 to RM8 and above, depending on the chosen design.
"Usually, there is an increase in customers two days before Deepavali because most of them come to decorate their hands with henna patterns in preparation for the celebration. At that time, it was indeed quite busy because customers come in succession, and some even make reservations to ensure they get their turn," she said.
Meanwhile, the Special Adviser on Indian Community Affairs in Negeri Sembilan, Datuk VS Mogan, said they expect more than 30,000 visitors to attend the 10-day carnival, with the bazaar featuring 140 traders offering various goods including clothing, traditional sweets and festival necessities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 13 foreigners arrested in Melaka over love scam, fake crypto exchange
Article:
MELAKA: Police have crippled an online scam syndicate involving "love scams" and a non-existent cryptocurrency exchange with the arrest of 13 foreigners at a house in Taman Kota Shahbandar yesterday.
Melaka Tengah police chief assistant commissioner Halim Abas said the suspects, consisting of 11 Chinese male nationals, one Taiwanese male national, and one Chinese female national aged between 24 and 36, were arrested in a raid about 3pm yesterday.
He said the syndicate targeted victims among Chinese nationals via the Telegram, QQ Chat, and Soul applications to deceive victims from China with sweet words and false promises.
"Initial investigations found that members of the syndicate entered Malaysia from the Philippines, Taiwan, Laos, and China by airplane between February and September last year.
"All suspects are believed to have used tourist visas to enter the country and started operating at the premises about three months ago," he said in a statement here today.
He said the syndicate deceived victims with sweet words and false promises and asked victims to transfer money in cryptocurrency exchange transactions that promised lucrative returns.
He said the total losses suffered by the syndicate's victims are still under investigation, and the police also seized 12 laptops of various brands, a desktop computer, 26 mobile phones, and a Unifi router, with a total estimated value of RM50,000.
Halim said all the suspects have been remanded for four days until Nov 8 to assist with the investigation under Section 420 of the Penal Code and Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
He said the public is also advised to check suspicious phone numbers or bank accounts via the Semak Mule portal at https://semakmule.rmp.gov.my.
"Scam victims can also contact the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) via the 997 hotline immediately to enable actions to block financial transactions to be taken," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MoE to maintain 12 weekly language teaching periods under 2027 curriculum
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry will retain 12 weekly teaching periods for Bahasa Melayu in national schools, Chinese in national-type Chinese schools and Tamil in national-type Tamil schools under the 2027 School Curriculum.
In a statement, the ministry said the decision followed engagement sessions with stakeholders on the allocation of language teaching periods under the new curriculum.
"The ministry appreciates the views and suggestions put forward during the discussions.
"After careful consideration and discussions, the ministry has decided to retain 12 weekly teaching periods for the languages concerned.
"This is to ensure that the allocation of teaching periods for these languages is not reduced," it said.
The ministry also thanked all parties who contributed their views during the engagement sessions.
"Language proficiency and the learning needs of pupils across all school streams remain a priority in the country's curriculum reform," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Retention pond overflow triggers flash floods in Saujana Utama
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH: Heavy rain triggered flash floods at Taman Seri Alam in Saujana Utama here today after a nearby water retention pond overflowed.
Floodwaters reached an estimated depth of one foot in the residential area, although no evacuations have been reported so far.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ahmad Ashrul Riezal Asbar said firefighters received a distress call at 5.48pm.
"A team of five firefighters from the Bestari Jaya Fire and Rescue Station arrived at the scene at 5.51pm.
"Upon arrival, firefighters found that heavy rain had caused flooding in the residential area following an overflow from a nearby water retention pond.
"Floodwaters were estimated to be one foot deep. No evacuations have been carried out so far," he said.
The incident came amid heavy rain affecting several areas in Puncak Alam and its surroundings, including Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Puncak Alam, Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari and Hill Park.
Earlier, firefighters were also dispatched to UiTM Puncak Alam following reports of flooding on the campus.
However, the floodwaters had fully receded by the time firefighters arrived, and no evacuation assistance was required.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 4 telcos ordered to improve internet services in Kuala Krau - Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Four telecommunications service providers have been directed to submit network improvement plans following complaints over poor Internet service quality in several areas of Kuala Krau, Pahang.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) issued compliance notices to the four providers on Nov 4 after quality tests and assessments found several locations requiring network upgrades.
"Tests conducted under the Mandatory Standards for Quality of Service (MSQoS) for wireless broadband access, along with assessments through MCMC Nexus, found that service quality in several locations required improvements by the relevant providers," he said during the Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
The minister was responding to Kamal Ashaari (PN-Kuala Krau), who raised concerns over the quality and stability of Internet coverage in several areas of the constituency.
Fahmi said MCMC conducted service quality audits at 17 locations in Kuala Krau between Jan 1 and Oct 31 this year, with seven meeting MSQoS requirements while the remaining 10 recorded a total of 20 instances of non-compliance.
Among the locations identified for network optimisation and upgrades were Masjid Kampung Gong Halt and Taman Desa Seroja in Kampung Paya Sok.
During the same period, Fahmi said MCMC received 28 complaints involving service disruptions and poor coverage in Kuala Krau, of which 16 had been resolved while 12 remained under investigation or follow-up action.
He said measures to address outstanding complaints included network optimisation, infrastructure sharing through the multi-operator core network (MOCN) system and the development of new telecommunications sites, subject to technical assessments and service providers' plans.
On infrastructure development, the minister said eight telecommunications tower sites had been planned for Kuala Krau under the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela), with seven completed and operational and the remaining site expected to be ready by March 2027.
According to MCMC Nexus data as of Oct 1, Kuala Krau recorded average download and upload speeds of 79.55 Mbps and 17.35 Mbps, respectively.
However, average download speeds in Kampung Gong Halt, Kampung Paya Sok and Kampung Sungai Mai were considerably lower at 18.75 Mbps, 12.13 Mbps and 37.53 Mbps, respectively.
Their corresponding upload speeds were 15.99 Mbps, 6.49 Mbps and 13.09 Mbps.
Fahmi said actual user experience could vary depending on distance from transmission towers, physical obstructions, network capacity, terrain and environmental conditions, including vegetation that could affect signal strength.
Meanwhile, he said the second phase of Jendela would be rolled out in stages beginning this month, involving 1,000 planned sites nationwide, including 57 in Pahang.
The rollout would cover 4G and 5G cellular services as well as satellite broadband, using technologies suited to population density, terrain and existing infrastructure.
Fahmi said 12 National Information Dissemination Centres (Nadi) were also operating in Kuala Krau, providing Internet access and programmes in digital skills, education and entrepreneurship.
As of Sept 1, the constituency had recorded 3,720 participations in the Nadi Tuisyen Rakyat programme and 4,889 in entrepreneurship programmes.

Title: PAC urged to probe alleged overspending by Rural Ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has been urged to investigate allegations that the Rural and Regional Development Ministry had exceeded its budget allocations for four consecutive years.
Chong Zhemin (PH-Kampar) said an investigation was necessary to prevent ministries from routinely overspending without being held accountable.
He said his call was not politically motivated, despite the ministry being led by an Umno minister.
"If every ministry overspends by 25 per cent and then asks the Treasury for additional allocations, what will happen?
"We have 30 ministries with an annual budget exceeding RM400 billion. If they overspend by 25 per cent, that means an additional RM100 billion in expenditure every year," he said while debating the 2027 Supply Bill at the committee stage in the Dewan Rakyat.
Chong questioned whether spending beyond approved allocations was permitted under financial regulations and whether action would be taken against the ministry.
He also sought a breakdown of outstanding commitments and projects allegedly cancelled in Sabah and Sarawak, including those that had been sacrificed because of the reported overspending.
Datuk Mohd Isam Mohd Isa (BN-Tampin), a PAC member, supported referring the matter to the committee for a full investigation.
Manndzri Nasib (BN-Tenggara), however, proposed that the investigation be extended to all ministries instead of focusing solely on the Rural and Regional Development Ministry.
Meanwhile, Wilfred Madius Tangau (GRS-Tuaran) called on the ministry to clarify the status of rural development projects in Sabah, following the Finance Ministry's explanation that projects previously reported as cancelled had only been postponed.
He said the ministry should identify the affected projects, their implementation status and when work would resume.
"The Finance Ministry has explained the issue of cancelled and postponed rural road projects in Sabah.
"Now, Tuaran is asking the Rural and Regional Development Ministry to clarify the actual situation.
"Have the projects been cancelled or will they proceed? If they are proceeding, when? Which projects are ongoing, which have been postponed and when will they resume? Will the affected projects in Sabah continue in 2027?" he asked.
Isnaraissah Munirah (Warisan-Kota Belud) also demanded a list of the affected projects.
"I just want to know which projects are involved," she said.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan previously told parliament that the ministry received an additional RM500 million for rural road projects this year, on top of RM491 million reallocated internally.
He said no approved projects were cancelled, although some tenders and contract awards were postponed to manage existing commitments and outstanding payments.
Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul had earlier asked Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi to explain alleged inconsistencies in his statements on the projects and submit supporting documents by Nov 12.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Experience with MIC leaders helps Nadarajah's campaign in Gadek
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: The experience of accompanying several MIC leaders during their campaigns and constituency work has helped Barisan Nasional candidate for Gadek, S. Nadarajah, prepare for the Melaka election.
He admitted that he was not feeling too pressured despite being the only MIC representative contesting in the election.
"In the past, I had the opportunity to accompany several MIC leaders. I was with them when they carried out their duties, campaigned and served as elected representatives.
"So, that experience has helped me a lot," he said when met after receiving a visit from Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh at the Gadek BN operations room here today.
Also present was MIC deputy president Datuk Seri M. Saravanan.
On his campaign, Nadarajah said he was satisfied with the efforts of the BN machinery in helping him reach out to voters.
He said meeting the people had also given him the opportunity to listen to their grievances, including complaints about unresolved issues.
"We need to listen patiently. Even when they are angry at times, we must listen. They are not angry with me, but are disappointed because the things they had hoped for have yet to be delivered.
"Before becoming a people's representative, one must first be among the people. I am going through that process now so that I can become a people's representative who is able to serve," he said.
On local issues, Nadarajah said flooding was among the problems frequently raised by residents during his visits to Gadek since he was appointed state MIC Youth chief in 2016.
He said Gadek had over 16,000 voters, with 49 per cent aged below 40.
He added that between 2,000 and 3,000 were new voters, including young people aged 18 and above as well as those who had moved into the constituency or changed their addresses to the area.
"We need to reach out to young people. Tok Rauf has already taken steps in this direction through the Gagasan Melaka Sayang Rakyat initiative, which includes various programmes for youths. These have helped our campaign this time," he said.
Nadarajah is facing a four-cornered contest in the Melaka election against Pakatan Harapan's Jegasilan Kungamboo, Bersama candidate B. Laveen and Laila Norinda Maon of Parti Bumiputera Perkasa Malaysia.
In the 2021 state election, BN's Datuk V. P. Shanmugam won the seat with a majority of 559 votes.

Title: Zahid: Gaza plight among issues Malaysia will raise at TRT World Forum
Article:
ISTANBUL: Malaysia will raise the ongoing conflict in Gaza at tomorrow's 2026 TRT World Forum, with Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi saying Turkiye could play a role in pushing for a resolution.
He said Malaysia was concerned was that the situation in Gaza remained unresolved.
"Turkiye has diplomatic relations with Israel and is in a position to influence not only the Israeli prime minister (Benjamin Netanyahu) but also the United States president (Donald Trump).
"As such, its role is important in helping resolve the Palestinian issue, not only on behalf of Muslim countries but also on humanitarian grounds," he told reporters after chairing a pre-council meeting with the Malaysian delegation here today.
On another matter, Zahid said Malaysia saw significant potential to expand trade ties with Turkiye, particularly in defence and security procurement.
He said Turkiye's advanced defence technology and its membership of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (Nato) offered opportunities for Malaysia to acquire equipment while benefiting from technology transfers and expertise-sharing.
Meanwhile, on education, Zahid said Universiti Kuala Lumpur (UniKL) under Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara), which falls directly under him, would explore opportunities to send students to Turkiye.
He said it would also invite its Turkish counterparts to conduct training for trainers at UniKL and Universiti Poly-Tech Malaysia (UPTM), which is also under Mara.
"I plan, through the National Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Council, which I chair, to send TVET students to Turkiye to master certain fields.
"Since Mara alone has 270 TVET institutions, I will identify critical aspects in line with the National TVET Policy 2.0, so that we include Turkiye as a country from which we can explore and learn in several fields," he said.
Tomorrow, Zahid will attend the forum's opening ceremony, to be officiated by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and will also speak at a session titled "Turkiye: From Regional Power to Multi-Regional Actor".
Malaysia and Turkiye established diplomatic relations on June 17, 1964, and have since maintained close ties in politics, the economy, trade and education.
Malaysia is one of Turkiye's largest trading partners in Southeast Asia.
Bilateral trade stands at US$5.6 billion, and both countries aim to raise it to US$10 billion by 2030 following an agreement between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Erdogan in January.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 5 Sarawak incumbents may sit out election over health issues
Article:
KUCHING: At least five incumbent assemblymen, including two deputy ministers in the Sarawak Cabinet, are expected to be dropped from the candidate line-up for the 13th Sarawak election due to health reasons, according to a source.
One of the assemblymen is said to be stepping down after suffering from a chronic illness that recently required him to undergo a leg amputation.
The two deputy ministers, including a woman, are also said to be in poor health and unlikely to contest in the upcoming election.
The development points to possible changes to Gabungan Parti Sarawak's (GPS) candidate line-up, particularly involving incumbents who are no longer able to fully discharge their responsibilities as elected representatives due to health problems.
However, GPS leaders have yet to officially confirm the identities of those who may not be renominated for the election.
The Election Commission is scheduled to hold a special meeting here tomorrow to discuss key dates for the Sarawak election, including nomination and polling days.
Yesterday, Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu deputy president Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the GPS candidate list would only be announced in the run-up to nomination day.
He said all four GPS component parties — Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu, Parti Rakyat Sarawak, Progressive Democratic Party and Sarawak United Peoples' Party — had agreed to leave the selection of candidates entirely to GPS caretaker chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg.
The decision gives Abang Johari the mandate to determine the coalition's candidates for all 82 state constituencies, including whether to field new faces to strengthen GPS's chances of retaining power.
With the candidate list expected to be announced only closer to nomination day, attention is now on Abang Johari's decision and the possible changes to GPS's line-up for the election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Driver rescued before trailer cabin catches fire in Klang
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A trailer driver was rescued moments before the vehicle caught fire after losing control and crashing into road dividers at Km11 of Jalan Pelabuhan Barat towards Klang early today.
South Klang police chief assistant commissioner Lim Jit Huey said the 58-year-old man was pulled out of the vehicle before the fire intensified and taken to Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital, Klang for treatment.
He said the incident occurred about 5.15am when the trailer is believed to have lost control, struck the left road divider before veering off and crashing into the centre divider.
"The impact caused the trailer's cargo section to detach completely from the cabin, resulting in the cabin catching fire," he said in a statement today.
Lim said firefighters brought the blaze under control at about 6.15am, while police managed traffic until the trailer was removed.
The case is being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Earlier, a video showing the trailer engulfed in flames and obstructing traffic along a road in front of a warehouse went viral on social media.

Title: Bomb threats force flights to land in France, Bulgaria, Belgium
Article:
PARIS: Bomb threats forced airliners to make unplanned landings across Europe on Thursday morning, the latest in a series of threats targeting flights in Europe.
Aer Lingus flight EI402 from Dublin to Rome landed safely at Evreux airport, 100km west of Paris, after being diverted as a security precaution, the Irish airline said in a statement.
Belgian media reported that an airliner forced to land at Brussels' Zaventem airport belonged to the Polish airline LOT.
A Finnair plane from Helsinki was safely escorted to its scheduled landing in Rome by the Italian air force, a source close to the matter said.
Bulgarian officials reported three aircraft making emergency landings because of bomb threats.
Airplanes flying from Copenhagen and Madrid landed in Sofia, the interior minister said, according to broadcaster bTV.
A third aircraft, from London, landed in Plovdiv, local media said.
On Tuesday, at least seven flights and a cruise ship received bomb threats, causing disruption at airports across Europe, although no devices were discovered.
While no country has attributed blame for the threats, ⁠they come at a time when European officials have been blaming both Russia and Iran for what they describe as "hybrid attacks" and acts of sabotage. Moscow and Teheran both deny any such campaign.
This week, unidentified hackers shut down fridges in supermarkets in several European countries. Some experts said hoax bomb threats could be part of a similar pattern of low-cost, ⁠deniable disruption efforts.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shortage of 513 nurses keeps Pasir Gudang Hospital wards closed
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A shortage of 513 nurses at Pasir Gudang Hospital (HPG) has left some wards unopened, preventing the facility from fully utilising its capacity.
State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the hospital currently had only 343 nurses against 856 approved positions.
He said the shortage persisted despite all 14 specialist services being operational.
"Medical officer staffing is almost fully filled, with only nine vacancies out of 197 approved positions.
"However, the nursing shortage remains critical and requires urgent intervention," he said after launching the Sungai Sengkuang, Segget and Danga river rehabilitation programme in Taman Sentosa here today.
Ling said overall staffing at HPG had improved to 52 per cent from 48 per cent in September.
He called on the Health Ministry to deploy more nurses and supporting healthcare personnel to enable all wards to operate and meet growing demand for medical services in the area.
HPG, located in Bandar Seri Alam, Masai, began phased operations on Aug 1 last year to ease congestion at Sultanah Aminah Hospital and Sultan Ismail Hospital.
The RM375.5 million hospital has 304 beds, 14 specialist services, 8 operating theatres, 30 dialysis stations and 16 delivery rooms.

Title: [UPDATED] Fire stations across Selangor ordered to monitor flood-prone areas
Article:
SHAH ALAM: All fire and rescue stations across Selangor have been instructed to conduct early flood monitoring as a precaution following heavy rainfall in several parts of the state today.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations division assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the directive included monitoring flood-prone areas such as Puncak Alam and Meru.
"All fire and rescue stations have been instructed to conduct early monitoring as part of flood mitigation efforts, including in Puncak Alam and Meru," he said.
He said the department had received reports of flooding at Hillpark, Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, Jalan Meru towards Puncak Alam and Taman Seri Alam.
Meanwhile, Ashrul said a team from the Bestari Jaya Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the kindergarten at Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Selangor's Puncak Alam campus following reports of flooding.
He said the department received a call at 5pm, with five firefighters arriving at the location at 5.26pm.
"Upon arrival, the operations commander found that the floodwaters had completely receded and there was no need to evacuate anyone from the building.
"Personnel were instructed to monitor the surrounding area to ensure conditions were safe," he said.
The situation was brought under control at 5.33pm, with the operation ending at 5.43pm.
No casualties were reported.

Title: Seven Johor rivers remain heavily polluted
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Seven rivers in Johor remain among the country's most polluted waterways, with water quality readings placing them in Class Four and Five categories.
However, the number has dropped significantly from 28 rivers recorded in the same categories in 2017.
Under the National Water Quality Standards, Class Three water requires extensive treatment before use, while Class Four water is suitable only for irrigation and Class Five is considered unsuitable for any beneficial use.
State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the affected rivers were Sungai Sengkuang, Sungai Segget, Sungai Danga, Sungai Tukang Batu, Sungai Kempas, Sungai Pandan and Sungai Tampoi.
He said a two-month pilot project using environmentally friendly eco-enzyme treatment had been launched at Sungai Sengkuang and Sungai Segget to improve their water quality.
Under the initiative, 500 litres of eco-enzyme will be poured into the 2 rivers every Thursday, while the Johor Baru City Council will collect water samples monthly for laboratory analysis.
"The two rivers were selected because they are located in the city centre and have shorter stretches compared with other rivers.
"If the treatment improves water quality, we will extend the initiative to other polluted rivers," he said after launching the Sungai Sengkuang, Segget and Danga river rehabilitation programme at Sungai Sengkuang, Taman Sentosa, here today.
Ling said the pilot phase would run for 2 months, followed by 6 months of monitoring to assess its effectiveness.
He said the state hoped the initiative would improve the rivers' water quality and eventually move them out of the polluted category into Class Three.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iskandar Investment charts next growth phase after RM6bil infrastructure investment
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Iskandar Investment Bhd (IIB) is targeting its next phase of growth under its STAR2040 strategy, focusing on attracting investments, strengthening business ecosystems and generating greater economic value for Johor.
The move comes as the company marks its 20th anniversary, having invested RM6 billion in enabling infrastructure to support the transformation of about 2,703 hectares of development land across Iskandar Puteri.
IIB president and chief executive officer Datuk Idzham Mohd Hashim said the company will build on two decades of investments and partnerships to position Iskandar Puteri as a competitive business and investment destination.
He said its focus would be on ensuring existing development foundations continued to attract businesses and deliver long-term value for Johor.
Since 2013, Medini has attracted 47 global business services companies, supporting about 7,200 jobs, while EduCity has produced nearly 10,000 graduates since opening in 2012.
IIB also reported RM816.7 million in revenue generated for local, state and federal governments through its development activities.
Its portfolio includes Medini, EduCity and the 1,200-hectare Wawari masterplan, with the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone expected to create further opportunities for cross-border business operations.
The company also unveiled a refreshed corporate identity with the tagline "Catalysing Growth", replacing its previous "Catalyst of Change" slogan, to reflect its evolving role in driving investment and economic development.

Title: Glove companies' earnings set to slip in Q3
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Glove makers' earnings are likely to decline in the third quarter (Q3) weighed down by average selling price (ASP) normalisation in Q2 and higher natural gas tariffs, said CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
The firm noted that ASP dropped to about US$22 per 1,000 pieces from between US$25 and US$28 per 1,000 pieces during the June quarter.
"Beyond Q3, we foresee further margin compression risk as the higher natural gas tariff of RM59/MMBtu takes effect, compared with the September quarter average of RM49.9/MMBtu.
"Natural gas typically accounts for 10–15 per cent of total glove production costs," said the firm.
CIMB Securities anticipates a potential increase in ASP by US$1/1,000 pieces driven by the recent surge in key input costs. This would bring the effective ASP to US$23.
"While this could support a modest improvement in Q4 earnings, we believe glove manufacturers are unlikely to replicate the peak core earnings achieved in the June quarter, as ASPs have normalised significantly from peak levels of approximately US$28/1,000 pieces in June," it said.
Additionally, implementing the minimum wage increase to RM2,000 from RM1,700, effective June 2027 is expected to negatively impact glove manufacturers' margins owing to the industry's labour-intensive nature and its continued reliance on a sizable blue-collar workforce.
Based on the firm's estimates, the increase in minimum wages could reduce earnings in the financial year 2027 (FY27) and FY28 by about four per cent and seven per cent respectively.
"We expect the global glove industry to remain oversupplied at least until 2027, driven by newly commissioned facilities across Southeast Asia that are estimated to add between 10 and 15 billion pieces of annual capacity in 2026.
"We estimate global glove demand growth of about three per cent in 2026, taking into account the weak US import data," it said.
Global glove demand growth is then expected to accelerate to 10 per cent in 2027 and seven per cent in 2028, broadly in line with the pre–Covid-19 five-year historical average of between 10 per cent and 12 per cent.
"With industry capacity expansion likely to outpace demand growth, we expect glove manufacturers under our coverage to face ongoing pricing pressure amid a still-unfavourable supply-demand environment," it said.
The firm maintained its "Neutral" call on the sector, given that persistent demand-supply imbalance and rising cost pressures could continue to weigh on margins.
The sector is currently trading at 0.9 times price-to-book ratio, near the valuation peak reached in May when ASPs were at their highest.
The firm remains Kossan Rubber Industries Bhd as its sector pick, supported by its relatively higher exposure to non-generic products and a strong net cash position equivalent to 49 per cent of its market capitalisation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Election of first Muslim to US Senate is lesson against racial politics, says Anwar
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 5 — The historic election of the first Muslim to the United States Senate should serve as a lesson for all on the importance of rejecting racial prejudice and religious discrimination, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He cited Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s victory in Michigan as an example of how political participation could transcend racial and religious differences.
Anwar said the development reflected growing political acceptance of diversity and demonstrated that democracy should provide opportunities for people of all backgrounds, rather than be driven by racial sentiment.
“They understand democracy and reject racism. Those who defeated President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the United States are people who oppose racism.
“They campaigned against racism and religious oppression, bringing a new message. When racism gains ground, Muslims and other minorities are the ones who suffer,” he said at the Melaka Madani Aspirations Tour programme for Klebang constituency at Taman Bukit Rambai here today.
El-Sayed, a Democrat, won Michigan’s Senate seat in the US midterm elections, becoming the first Muslim elected to the Senate.
Anwar said the victory demonstrated how rejecting racial prejudice could become a powerful message for political change.
However, he stressed that Malaysia need not emulate the US political model, as the country had its own identity as a prosperous, multiracial nation. — Bernama

Title: Zahid urges ‘respect’ between BN, Perikatan as Melaka campaigning intensifies
Article:
ISTANBUL, Nov 5 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has reminded all party machinery to exercise restraint and conduct their campaigning responsibly during the 16th Melaka State Election.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said that while campaigning between BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) had intensified, there had also been several clashes that should have been avoided.
“My stand, as well as that of the chairman of the coalition on the other side (PN), is that we should respect what we have mutually agreed upon.
“Although there is no formal agreement, mutual understanding is very important,” he told Malaysian media after a pre-meeting with the country’s representatives and delegation in conjunction with his working visit to Turkiye here today.
Ahmad Zahid said excessive campaigning, including raising issues unrelated to the state election, would not change the stance or decisions already made by voters.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting will take place on November 10.
For the latest news on the Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama
