Title: Tengku Puteri Zainah, former wife of Najib, dies at 70
Article:
KUANTAN, Nov 5 — Tengku Puteri Zainah Tengku Eskandar, the mother of Pahang Investment, Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation Committee chairman Datuk Mohamad Nizar Najib, died today. She was 70.
Mohamad Nizar, who is also the Peramu Jaya assemblyman, shared the sad news in a post on his Facebook page.
“It is with deep sorrow that I announce the passing of my beloved mother, Tengku Puteri Zainah,” the post read.
The eldest son of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak also expressed his appreciation for his mother’s love, sacrifices, and prayers.
“Nothing can ever repay all your deeds. May
Allah
forgive all your sins, grant His mercy, and place you among the dwellers of heaven.
“Mother, you’ll remain in my prayers and memories forever.
Al-Fatihah
,” he wrote.
Tengku Puteri Zainah had previously been reported to be in critical condition while receiving treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) of a hospital in the capital. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar: No reason to keep CSA secret, Cabinet to discuss disclosure tomorrow
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 5 — The government has no objection to disclosing the contents of the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) signed between the Unity Government, Bersatu and independent Members of Parliament, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said there was no reason to keep the agreement confidential and that he would raise the matter with Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, who oversees the arrangement, at tomorrow’s Cabinet meeting for further action.
“I have no objection to making it public. In fact, the draft and principles are similar to the agreement between Pakatan Harapan and the previous government comprising PAS, Bersatu and Umno.
“It was their party (PAS) that proposed such an agreement in the first place, together with Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin and several others in the government at the time.
“Yet they are now questioning it. It is rather strange when their own members have not read or thought about it,” he told reporters after officiating the Prime Minister’s Golden Hand Awards 2026 ceremony at Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) here today.
Anwar was responding to PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan’s call for the government to disclose the contents of the agreement.
Asked about PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s description of the CSA as a “devilish approach”, Anwar said the remark was inappropriate.
“Tan Sri Hadi is a religious scholar, and his statements should be more measured. He tried to explain that his remarks were not directed at me, and that is fine, but it is inappropriate to label a person, group, or position as devilish.
“How is it that when they do it, it is not devilish, but when others do the same, it becomes devilish? I do not think religion should be used in that manner,” he said.
On October 29, the Madani Government signed a CSA with six Bersatu MPs led by party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and seven others, including Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman. — Bernama

Title: Nilai teen tests positive for three drugs after dazed vaping video prompts police investigation
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 5 — A male secondary school student in Nilai has tested positive in a preliminary urine screening for three types of drugs, namely ketamine, benzodiazepines and THC.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the 17-year-old student was being investigated following the circulation of a video on social media showing him allegedly in a dazed state after vaping.
Alzafny said the video was believed to have been circulated on October 28 at a secondary school in the district.
“Police took note of the video circulating on the Threads platform on November 4 before launching an investigation and identifying the student involved.
“However, the preliminary urine screening results are still subject to further confirmation. In this regard, a police report has been lodged in connection with the incident,” he said in a statement here today.
Alzafny said the student would be referred to the National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) for further action under Section 3(1) of the Drug Dependants (Treatment and Rehabilitation) Act 1983. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak eyes 2050 plan to spread jobs, services and growth beyond major cities
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 5 — Sarawak is considering a long-term urban development policy through 2050 to guide settlement planning and ensure balanced development across major cities, smaller towns and rural areas.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the proposed Sarawak Urban Development Policy 2050 would provide long-term direction for the state's urban and settlement system, taking into account its vast geographical landscape and diverse communities.
He said the policy should be aligned with statutory plans, development decisions, infrastructure programmes and accountable delivery arrangements to ensure that strategic planning translates into effective implementation.
“Through the Post COVID-19 Development Strategy 2030, we seek to advance economic prosperity, social inclusivity and environmental sustainability as mutually reinforcing objectives,” he said.
He said this during his closing keynote address titled “Leadership for Better Cities: Our Shared Responsibility”, at the 11th National Planning Congress 2026, Dewan Sivik Majlis Bandaraya Petaling Jaya, here today.
Elaborating further, Abang Johari said Sarawak recognised the importance of developing a strong settlement system that connected urban centres with their surrounding regions.
“Kuching, Sibu, Bintulu, Miri and our growing towns should play complementary roles in providing services, employment and economic opportunity,” he added.
Abang Johari said development planning should also take into account the different needs of smaller towns, riverine settlements, rural communities and interior areas.
He noted the state should not expect every settlement to become a metropolitan centre, but instead ensure that each had access to appropriate services, connectivity and economic opportunities.
He emphasised that strategic plans must guide land use, transport, housing, public facilities and environmental protection in a coordinated manner, with clear outcomes, responsible agencies and the necessary resources for implementation.
“We do not claim to have solved every challenge...but we believe consistent policy direction, institutional cooperation and a commitment to measurable outcomes provide the foundation for progress,” he said.
Abang Johari said the true measure of development was whether it delivered tangible benefits to the people, such as shorter journeys to work, better homes, more reliable public services, safer neighbourhoods and lower household expenses. — Bernama

Title: RM1.5m facelift for Penang Assembly includes heritage gallery, lactation room and upgraded media area
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 5 — The Penang State Legislative Assembly has implemented several infrastructure improvements and upgrading works at its building here, involving a cost of RM1.5 million.
This was undertaken in conjunction with the Second Meeting of the Fourth Session of the 15th Penang State Legislative Assembly.
Its Speaker, Datuk Seri Law Choo Kiang, said the works involved improvements to both the interior and exterior of the building, including a comprehensive structural inspection through a dilapidation report and roof maintenance.
He said among the new facilities provided was a dedicated lactation room for breastfeeding mothers, in addition to improvements to the staff rest area to provide a more comfortable environment with greater privacy.
“In addition, the State Assembly Building Gallery has been rebranded as ‘Warisan Visual Terukir’ (Engraved Visual Heritage) to showcase the history and contributions of Penang State Assemblymen who have served from 1959 to 2026,” he said in a statement today.
He said the upgrading efforts also included the provision of a Special Officers’ Room equipped with workspaces, printing facilities and audio-visual equipment, as well as improvements to the State Assembly Meeting Room, which can now accommodate up to 25 people at any one time.
Law said the special media conference area had also been upgraded to provide greater comfort for media practitioners covering the assembly sitting.
The upgrading works will continue after the sitting concludes, including improvements to the disabled-friendly toilet near the guardhouse and the renovation of the general storeroom to ensure that equipment used during assembly sittings can be stored in a more orderly and organised manner. — Bernama

Title: Batu Caves ritual video: Youth repents publicly with family at Shah Alam mosque
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 5 — A 21-year-old Muslim youth whose participation in Hindu rituals at a Batu Caves temple sparked a controversy made a public declaration of repentance today alongside his mother and younger sister, prior to undergoing court-ordered faith rehabilitation.
Reciting the Islamic declaration of faith before state religious officials at the Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Mosque here, Aliff Daniel Adli renounced the Hindu and Buddhist rituals he had previously engaged in, acknowledging that his actions violated Islamic tenets and caused widespread distress.
“I once again declare that, without coercion from any party and in good faith, by uttering the words, ‘There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah’, I repent to Allah with sincere and genuine repentance,” he said during the ceremony, vowing not to repeat the acts and committing to study Islamic doctrine under qualified religious guidance.
His mother, Rohizayanti Ramli, and younger sister, Nur Ranea Ezreen Adli, made their own formal declarations of repentance, expressing regret over failing to guide and counsel him away from external influences that conflicted with Islamic teachings.
An emotional Rohizayanti admitted that parental lapses and a lack of religious grounding had contributed to her son's misstep.
“I acknowledge all forms of negligence, carelessness and shortcomings in fulfilling my fundamental duties and responsibilities as a mother,” she said, pledging to attend religious classes and work closely with Islamic authorities to guide her son.
Nur Ranea similarly expressed remorse for not providing adequate advice to shield her brother from external influences, committing to support him through prayer, family care, and ongoing cooperation with religious bodies.
Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said the public ceremony was held to confirm that all three family members have genuinely repented and returned to the fold of Islam in accordance with Ahli Sunnah Wal Jamaah teachings, while easing community anger following the viral video clips.
“We want to demonstrate through this declaration that he has genuinely repented. Hopefully, Muslims who were initially angry or disappointed with Aliff Daniel will realise that we are all human and we make mistakes.
“We can now see for ourselves that Aliff Daniel has repented and wants to return to the teachings of Islam,” he said at a brief press conference later.
Salehuddin disclosed that the Syariah Court has ordered Aliff Daniel to undergo three months of mandatory faith rehabilitation at Pusat Pemurnian Akidah Baitul Iman in Hulu Yam, Selangor.
During his stay, he will receive structured Islamic instruction from accredited teachers, followed by long-term monitoring and pastoral guidance from the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS).
The MAIS chairman expressed hope that Aliff Daniel would eventually help encourage his mother and sister to attend regular classes at their neighbourhood mosque, while urging social media users who may have been influenced by his past posts to disavow any practices that run counter to Islamic teachings.

Title: Ramanan: Mitra allocates RM755,390 to upgrade facilities at 21 Tamil schools in Melaka
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 5 — The Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra) has allocated RM755,390 to 21 Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Tamil (SJKT) in Melaka this year to enhance teaching and learning facilities.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the allocation covered various initiatives, including MADANI furniture assistance, tuition classes and digital learning tools such as smartboards.
“The programmes are implemented through collaboration between Mitra and the Education Ministry, as well as school administrators and boards of governors, to ensure students benefit from the assistance,” he said during a visit to SJKT Jasin Lalang in Ayer Merbau here today.
Ramanan said SJKT Jasin Lalang had received RM47,560 under the initiatives.
He said Mitra had also introduced various educational assistance programmes this year for Indian students at all levels, from preschool to public and private higher education institutions.
“Our approach covers the entire education ecosystem to ensure targeted groups receive assistance tailored to their needs at every stage of learning.
“These initiatives also focus on expanding access to technology and digitalisation in schools,” he added. — Bernama

Title: No transfer letter received, Shuhaily remains border agency chief, lawyer says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Embattled Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MBCA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has yet to receive an official transfer letter from the Home Ministry, leaving him legally empowered to lead the agency despite ministerial statements that he is being returned to the police force.
Counsel Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali confirmed that in the absence of a formal administrative directive, his client remains fully authorised to execute his duties at the helm of the national border agency,
FMT
reported.
“To date, he has not been found guilty of any offence. He can therefore continue to carry out his duties as usual,” he said when met at the court complex here.
Rafique called on Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail to address the administrative ambiguity, arguing that public pronouncements of an impending transfer had generated confusion and invited unnecessary speculation.
“People are now questioning why the minister has announced one thing while what is happening on the ground suggests otherwise. Saifuddin should clarify this matter as it has given rise to speculation,” he said.
The clarification follows Saifuddin's announcement last week that the Home Ministry had decided to terminate Shuhaily's secondment to MBCA and return him to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
However, despite being described as “on leave” the preceding week, Shuhaily returned to active duty on Monday, formally chairing an MBCA commanders' operational meeting.
Shuhaily, who formerly headed Bukit Aman’s Criminal Investigation Department, was seconded to lead MBCA on a two-year contract commencing July 1 last year.
His tenure was thrust into the spotlight after he claimed trial at the Sepang Magistrate's Court on Oct 21 to two counts of voluntarily causing hurt under Section 323 of the Penal Code, involving an alleged altercation with two Special Branch officers at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in late September.
Any premature termination of his posting also faces a constitutional hurdle.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail previously clarified that because Shuhaily's two-year tenure was granted with the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, any decision to truncate his contract requires the formal assent of the King before taking legal effect.

Title: Govt expands Sabah sea surveillance system to plug maritime monitoring gaps
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 —  The government has approved the expansion of the Sabah Sea Surveillance System (Swasla) under Phase Two to cover Malawali Island and Sandakan, in a move to enhance the country’s maritime surveillance capabilities, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the project was approved under the First Rolling Plan of the 13th Malaysia Plan for 2026 to address gaps in maritime surveillance coverage across Malaysian waters, with the tender process expected to begin by year-end.
He said the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) currently operates 15 Remote Sensored Site (RSS) radar stations under Swasla, comprising 12 along the Strait of Melaka and three off Sabah’s west coast.
“All 15 MMEA RSS stations operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, providing continuous surveillance within their respective coverage areas,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam) on early detection systems using radar, drones and satellites, round-the-clock surveillance coverage, smuggling syndicates dismantled and gaps in MMEA’s capabilities.
However, Shamsul Anuar said the radar stations’ continuous operation did not provide complete surveillance coverage of Malaysian waters, with MMEA deploying ships and boats to patrol areas beyond the system’s coverage.
He said funding for SWASLA development in Sarawak was approved under the Fourth Rolling Plan of the 12th Malaysia Plan (12MP) for 2024, while the proposed study on the system was still awaiting feedback from the Economy Ministry.
Shamsul Anuar said the government had also approved a study on SWASLA development along the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia under the Fourth Rolling Plan of the 12MP, with the tender process for the study to begin soon.
To strengthen maritime surveillance, he said the Home Ministry (KDN), through MMEA, was shifting from a “detect-and-act” approach to a more integrated system based on early detection, target identification and rapid response.
He said the approach involved expanding radar coverage, deploying unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), modernising assets and improving the integration of operational information, as well as procuring two UAV-equipped vessels to strengthen aerial surveillance capabilities.
Shamsul Anuar said MMEA has yet to acquire a dedicated satellite for continuous maritime surveillance, with existing satellite technology mainly used to support search and rescue (SAR) operations.
He said MMEA recorded 834 smuggling cases involving seizures worth RM257.55 million from 2020 to August this year.
However, he stressed that enforcement effectiveness was not measured solely by the number of seizures.
Instead, the government was focusing on dismantling the entire smuggling chain through detection, investigation, seizures, prosecution and intelligence sharing, while also targeting logistics networks and those supporting such activities, he said.
“Among the gaps in MMEA’s asset capabilities that still need to be addressed are incomplete surveillance coverage, the need for additional UAVs and aerial assets for continuous monitoring, long-range vessels, high-speed interception assets and a C4ISR (command, control, communications, computers, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance) system.
“The government is gradually addressing these gaps by expanding the Swasla network, procuring strategic assets and implementing programmes to modernise MMEA’s operational vessels and boats,” he said.
Responding to a supplementary question from Hasni on the detention and deportation of migrants entering Malaysian waters illegally, Shamsul Anuar said MMEA does not have its own detention centres but only lock-up facilities to hold suspects for remand and investigation purposes.
He said those sentenced would be transferred to the relevant authorities for placement in detention centres. — Bernama

Title: Liew Chin Tong urges accountants to embrace multidisciplinary skills as AI reshapes finance profession
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong has urged accountants and finance professionals to be multidisciplinary as the positive and negative impacts of artificial intelligence (AI) emerge and continue to occupy the minds of finance leaders in the years ahead.
He said AI would displace some less sophisticated jobs held by accountants but would probably create new ones requiring deeper human judgement, fewer technical skills and more value-based decision-making.
“It is in this context that I would say that Malaysia’s positioning in this less innocent and more complex era is to focus on ‘the three middles’.
“Namely, to fortify Malaysia’s position as the indispensable middle in the supply chain and in technology; to hold on to the geopolitical middle and be non-aligned throughout; and to build a strong middle class,” he said in his keynote address at the Certified Practising Accountant (CPA) Congress 2026 today.
He said that in 2026, an accountant or finance leader would be nearing dereliction of his or her duties if no attention were paid to geopolitics and geoeconomics, supply chain resilience, critical materials and minerals, technology and AI, and carbon emissions and climate change.
Liew said Malaysia, Asean and even Australia should see themselves as middle powers, adding that greater alignment among these countries would strengthen their ability to deal with superpowers, including the United States (US), China and Russia, on a more equal footing.
“But the US middle class is shrinking, and would not be able to consume the world’s entire manufacturing capacity. ASEAN states would need to create a sizable middle class rich enough to consume the outputs from the productive capacity in the region,” he said.
He said building and sustaining the middle class would require Southeast Asian nations to abandon a race-to-the-bottom mentality, work together to establish a floor on wages, create more homegrown technology corporations and increase local ownership of technology.
“Often, accountants and finance leaders are asked by their multinational clients or employers to urge ASEAN governments to compete with each other for favourable tax incentives, or suppression of wages or workers’ rights, or relaxed environmental laws and compliance requirements.
“I urge the accountants and the finance leaders in the room to resist such race-to-the-bottom acts as we have a collective objective to see a prosperous, cohesive, and safe Asean people,” he said.
Meanwhile, Liew said he had visited the Malaysian Institute of Accountants last week to discuss the long-awaited amendments to the Accountants Act 1967, which will mark its 60th anniversary in 2027.
“I hope we will be able to move the agenda to amend the law as quickly as possible. In the meantime, I hope to see discussion reflecting on six decades of the current legislation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: No water found in RON95 so far, but Petron and Caltex are offering goodwill payment to motorists with damaged engines
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Petron and Chevron, which operates the Caltex brand, have begun making goodwill payments to motorists whose vehicles suffered engine damage following complaints of contaminated RON95 petrol, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the compensation measures were initiated on a goodwill basis for verified complaints while investigations into the incidents continued.
“Caltex and Petron have initiated customer recovery programmes offering compensation on a goodwill basis based on established criteria, without any admission of wrongdoing or liability at this stage.
“Payments will be made to customers who have submitted complete complaints with valid supporting documents,” he said during Ministers’ Question Time.
The minister was responding to Abdul Latiff Abdul Rahman (PN-Kuala Krai), who sought the Chemistry Department’s findings on RON95 samples collected from five states and oil depots, as well as measures to restore consumer confidence and compensate affected motorists.
On the investigation, Armizan said preliminary analysis of 43 petrol samples by the Chemistry Department had found no evidence of water contamination.
He said an initial report dated Oct 29 showed water content below 0.05 per cent, the laboratory’s minimum reportable detection limit.
“The remaining samples are still being analysed, and a full report will be issued once the department completes its tests.
“The immediate focus was on detecting water contamination, but none has been found so far. We are now examining the possible presence of other foreign substances and the fuel formulation during the period concerned,” he said.
Armizan said 262 RON95 petrol samples had been collected from eight states and three oil company depots since complaints first emerged on Oct 3.
Both companies had also sent samples to their own laboratories, including those overseas, for further testing.
“Although the findings are not yet conclusive, the issue does not appear to affect the entire supply chain but rather fuel supplied during a specific period,” he said.
Armizan stressed that the incidents were not being treated as isolated cases, despite being concentrated in certain locations and periods, particularly in Kedah and Penang.
He said some affected petrol stations remained closed.
To prevent similar incidents, the ministry was benchmarking Malaysia’s fuel quality standards and supply chain monitoring practices against those of Singapore, the United Kingdom and Australia.
Armizan said motorists dissatisfied with the compensation offered could pursue other avenues, including lodging formal complaints with the ministry, filing civil suits or referring their cases to the Tribunal for Consumer Claims Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: Two Thai nationals face death penalty for allegedly killing MMEA officer in Sungai Padang
Article:
KANGAR, Nov 5 — Two Thai nationals were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with the murder of a Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) officer late last month.
No plea was recorded from Pradit Rimat, 22, and Rotchahan Tehpuyu, 21, after the charge was read to them in Thai by an interpreter before Magistrate Ana Rozana Mohd Nor, as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
Both accused were jointly charged with the murder of Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan, 41, near the Malaysian Fisheries Development Authority jetty in Sungai Padang here between 11 pm on Oct 26 and 1.30 am on Oct 27.
The charge was framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same Code, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and not less than 12 strokes of the cane if not sentenced to death, upon conviction.
The court did not allow bail and set Jan 5 next year for mention, pending the post-mortem and chemical reports.
MMEA deputy public prosecutors (DPPs) Wirna Arifin and Kamaliza Md Zain appeared for the prosecution, while both accused are unrepresented.
Meanwhile, at the Sessions Court before Judge Sharifah Norazlita Syed Salim Idid, the two men also faced a charge of smuggling nine Myanmar migrants using an unregistered boat.
Neither accused pleaded to that charge, which was alleged to have been committed in the waters off the mouth of Sungai Padang here between 11 pm on Oct 26 and 12.30 am on Oct 27.
The charge was framed under Section 26J of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of up to five years or a fine not exceeding RM250,000, or both, upon conviction.
However, in the same court, both accused pleaded guilty to entering Malaysia through an ungazetted route at the same location and time.
The charge was framed under Section 5(2), read together with Section 56(1A)(a) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, which provides for a fine not exceeding RM10,000 or imprisonment of up to five years, or both, upon conviction.
DPP Nur Afiqah Zakaria applied for a new mention date for the immigration case, as the prosecution is still awaiting the relevant documents from the Malaysian Immigration Department.
Judge Sharifah Norazlita fixed Dec 15 for mention of both the smuggling and immigration cases, and set the same date for the appointment of a Myanmar interpreter.
The interpreter is for seven Myanmar nationals, including a woman, who were charged with entering the country illegally.
The court did not allow bail for the Thai men and Myanmar nationals. — Bernama

Title: Takiyuddin: CSA funding terms must be made public like 2021 MoU
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) chief whip Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan today demanded full transparency over the recent Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) signed by 13 Opposition MPs, questioning the delay in terms disclosure, implementation details, and allocation figures.
Speaking at a press conference in Parliament, the Kota Bharu MP drew a contrast between the current pact signed on October 31 and the historic 2021 bipartisan Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed under the Ismail administration, which explicitly guaranteed public disclosure and equal constituency funding.
“Clause 6 stated there was no confidentiality. The parties agreed to fully disclose the memorandum to the public as a commitment to full openness and accountability. Right after it was signed, we published it immediately,” Takiyuddin said.
“We want to know whether the agreement signed on October 31 has been revealed to the public.”
He stressed that under the 2021 agreement, all Opposition MPs involved were allocated funding equivalent to government lawmakers.
“During our administration, we clearly stated in the MoU that funding equal to government Dewan Rakyat members would be allocated and disbursed to all participating MPs. All Pakatan Harapan MPs in 2021 received equal allocations,” he said.
Takiyuddin also revealed that an earlier draft proposal sent by Deputy Prime Minister  Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof on August 1 had left crucial funding details blank.
“It only stated that Constituency Development Funds (CDF) would be provided according to governance regulations, with the amount listed under Schedule C. But Schedule C was never provided to us,” he said.
Confirming that 62 Opposition MPs were not offered the CSA deal, Takiyuddin urged the government to disclose what was agreed upon with the 13 signatories.
“We demand full disclosure on what was signed on October 31 — how much allocation is given, the mechanism involved, and when it will be implemented,” he said.
But several news reports from October citing government leaders indicate agreement to disburse equal CDF to the 13 MPs upon the passage of Budget 2027 in Parliament.
Fadillah and Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz led the Madani government’s CSA negotiations.
The agreement entails support for the Anwar government’s push for institutional reforms,  including the two-term limit on the prime minister’s tenure and separating the attorney general’s roles.

Title: Driving home for Deepavali? 3.28 million vehicles expected daily on PLUS and major highways
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — About 3.28 million vehicles are expected to use major highways nationwide daily during the peak travel period for the Deepavali celebration this Sunday.
Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) director-general Ir Mohd Hadzmir Yusoff said traffic volume is expected to increase from today as motorists head towards the East Coast and the northern and southern parts of the country.
He said the PLUS highway network is projected to record 2.24 million vehicles, followed by the Duta-Ulu Kelang Expressway (DUKE) with 288,000 and the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway (KLK) with 190,000.
The West Coast Expressway (WCE) is expected to record 168,000 vehicles, while the Kuala Lumpur-Kuala Selangor Expressway (LATAR) and the Kajang-Seremban Expressway (LEKAS) are each projected to see 135,000 vehicles.
“The East Coast Expressway Phase 1 (LPT1) is projected to record 83,000 vehicles, while the East Coast Expressway Phase 2 (LPT2) is expected to see 44,000 vehicles,” he said in a statement here today.
Meanwhile, Mohd Hadzmir said LLM welcomed the government’s initiative to offer a toll discount of about 50 per cent for Class 1 vehicles (Class 2 on the Penang Bridge) for two days, from 12.01 am tomorrow until 11.59 pm on Saturday (Nov 7).
The discount applies to all highways nationwide, except at the Sultan Iskandar Building (BSI) Toll Plaza and the Tanjung Kupang Toll Plaza on the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link (LINKEDUA).
To ensure smooth traffic flow, Mohd Hadzmir said highway concessionaires have been instructed to temporarily halt all maintenance work requiring lane closures from Nov 6 to 10, except in emergencies.
“Highway concessionaires have also been instructed to provide additional facilities, including parking spaces and portable toilets, at several major rest and service areas (R&Rs), as well as ensure cleanliness and adequate water and fuel supplies for the convenience of highway users,” he said.
In a separate statement, PLUS Malaysia Berhad (PLUS) said traffic is expected to increase from today as motorists head back to their hometowns or travel to holiday destinations.
“Traffic towards the Klang Valley is expected to increase on Nov 9 and 10 as highway users return from their Deepavali and school holiday trips,” it said.
As such, PLUS advised motorists to plan their journeys in advance and refer to the MyPLUS Travel Time Advisory (MyPLUS-TTA) to determine the best time to travel.
PLUS said it has also activated Smart Lanes at 32 selected locations, allowing motorists to use designated emergency lanes temporarily to ease traffic congestion.
To facilitate smoother traffic flow at toll plazas, motorists are encouraged to use JustGO, Malaysia’s first Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR)-based toll payment system, available at all PLUS toll plazas except the BSI Toll Plaza and those on the LPT2 highway.
For motorists heading to the East Coast, AFA Prime Berhad (AFA Prime), the concessionaire for KLK and LPT1, has activated its Travel Time Advisory (TTA) schedule to ease congestion at key entry points, particularly the Gombak, Bentong and Jabor toll plazas.
AFA Prime Berhad managing director and chief executive officer Ahmad Faizi Latifi Ahmad Faiz encouraged highway users to travel during off-peak hours, between midnight and 6 am on both days, for smoother journeys.
The public can obtain the latest traffic updates through the official X accounts of PLUS (@plustrafik) and LLM (@llminfotrafik), or contact the toll-free PLUSLine at 1-800-88-0000 for emergency assistance. Real-time traffic images are also available on the LLM website at https://www.llm.gov.my. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s daily afternoon downpour returns with a 10-state thunderstorm warning
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has again issued an afternoon thunderstorm advisory for multiple states across the country, forecasting heavy downpours, lightning, and gusty winds until 4.00pm today.
The advisory, issued at 1.50pm, blankets wide sections of Peninsular Malaysia alongside extensive divisions in Sabah and Sarawak.
In the northern peninsula, stormy weather is expected across five Kedah districts: Baling, Sik, Kulim, Bandar Baharu, and Kuala Muda. The warning concurrently extends across mainland Penang through Seberang Perai Utara, Seberang Perai Tengah, and Seberang Perai Selatan, while Perak faces widespread disruption across nine districts, namely Kerian, Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, and Muallim.
In the central and southern corridors, localized downpours are forecast for Kuala Langat and Sepang in Selangor, alongside Putrajaya and the entire state of Melaka.
In Pahang, Rompin and Bera have been placed on alert. Across Negeri Sembilan, the warning spans Port Dickson, Rembau, Jempol, and Tampin, while in Johor, adverse weather is expected across Pontian, Batu Pahat, Segamat, Tangkak, and Muar.
Across East Malaysia, the bulletin covers central Sarawak divisions, including Betong, Mukah, Sarikei (incorporating Maradong), and Sibu (including Selangau).
In Sabah, severe conditions are anticipated across large parts of the West Coast, spanning Kota Belud, Tuaran, Penampang, Papar, Putatan, and Kota Kinabalu. Storms are also forecast in Kudat, alongside the Sandakan division (covering Sandakan, Kinabatangan, Paitan, and Labuk & Sugut) and the Tawau division (encompassing Semporna, Tawau, Lahad Datu, and Kunak).
MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warnings when satellite and radar indicators track rainfall intensity exceeding 20mm per hour that is either imminent or expected to persist beyond an hour.
The department noted that these bulletins serve as short-term alerts with a maximum validity of six hours from issuance.
Members of the public in affected localities are advised to remain vigilant, steer clear of open grounds, and take precautions against localized flash floods, sudden wind squalls, and falling roadside trees.

Title: Daiso’s largest global distribution centre on Pulau Indah a vote of confidence in Malaysia, says Anwar
Article:
PORT KLANG, Nov 5 — The decision by Japanese retail giant Daiso to establish its largest global distribution centre (GDC) on Pulau Indah, Selangor, reflects international confidence in Malaysia’s economic stability, infrastructure and long-term potential, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
He said such investments reflected Malaysia’s ability to leverage its strategic location, established port infrastructure and skilled workforce to attract companies looking to strengthen their global supply chains.
“Most of you present here, and I am sure many Malaysians, have possibly bought something from Daiso: a measuring cup, a storage box, a piece of stationery.
“But behind those low prices is one of the most complex supply chains in retail.
“So when a company like Daiso chooses Pulau Indah here for its largest GDC worldwide, it must certainly convey a profound message about the company and about this country.
“It is a resounding vote of confidence in Malaysia’s economic stability, infrastructure maturity and long-term potential,” he said at the GDC’s opening ceremony here.
Anwar, who noted that Port Klang ranked among the world’s 10 busiest container ports after handling a record 15.1 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) last year, said the GDC would enable goods arriving from around the world to be sorted, stored and repacked on Pulau Indah before being distributed to international markets.
He added that the GDC would allow Malaysia to capture a greater share of the value generated by global trade, rather than merely serving as a transit hub for cargo.
“A GDC like this is built around our ports, roads and people, and once it becomes part of a global supply chain, it stays for the long haul,” he said.
Anwar said the federal government was continuing to strengthen the country’s logistics ecosystem through investments in port, rail and air cargo infrastructure.
These include Westports II, which is expected to nearly double the port’s current capacity, and the proposed megaport on Pulau Carey, Selangor.
“Now, in many ways, this GDC is a microcosm of Malaysia’s trade story.
“Goods arrive from around the world, gain value on Malaysia’s shores and leave for markets far beyond.
“The Strait of Malacca have steered commercial flows for centuries. Our ambition is to expand it across land, sea and air to make Malaysia a world-class logistics hub,” he said.
He also commended Daiso for completing the new GDC ahead of schedule and below budget, describing it as an example of effective collaboration between the private sector and Malaysia’s public service.
Also present was Daiso Industries Co Ltd president and chief executive Seiji Yano.
Meanwhile, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said Daiso’s decision to locate its GDC near Port Klang demonstrated the National Transport Policy in action and highlighted the strategic importance of the country’s maritime and overland transport infrastructure.
“Daiso’s decision to build the largest logistics hub in the company’s history on Pulau Indah carries tremendous significance.
“It sends an unequivocal signal to the world that Malaysia is the regional supply chain and logistics hub of choice,” he said.
With an investment of RM1.2 billion, the Pulau Indah GDC is now Daiso’s largest warehouse globally, spanning 133,666 square metres and surpassing the size of its home base in Hiroshima, Japan.
It will serve as Daiso’s primary inbound and outbound logistics hub, connecting manufacturing operations across Japan, China and other global suppliers to 27 countries throughout Asia and the Middle East.

Title: Govt open to stronger support framework for SMEs moving beyond initial growth, says Fadillah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The government welcomes the business community’s proposal for more structured support for growth-stage small and medium enterprises (SMEs), said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
He said the proposal merited further consideration and constructive engagement with the relevant ministries, agencies and industry stakeholders.
“It is in this spirit that I welcome the suggestion to explore a more structured approach towards supporting growth-stage SMEs.
“Naturally, any proposed approach must be carefully assessed on its merits, taking into account existing initiatives and the practical needs of our businesses,” he said in his speech at the opening of the World Marketing Summit Malaysia 2026 here today.
Fadillah said equal attention must be given to helping businesses sustain their growth after achieving initial success.
He said securing a major contract or an opportunity to enter international markets could require an enterprise to recruit more employees, strengthen management capabilities, invest in equipment and obtain additional financing.
“The very opportunity that promises to take a business to greater heights can also test its ability to sustain that growth.
“We need to listen to entrepreneurs when shaping policies, as their experience in building businesses and overcoming challenges could help identify where support would make the greatest difference,” he said.
On artificial intelligence (AI), Fadillah said technology adoption should be guided by its ability to solve problems and serve people better.
“Are we adopting technology simply because it is available, or because it genuinely helps us solve a problem and serve people better?
“Meaningful innovation for small businesses does not necessarily require the most sophisticated technology, but may involve reducing time spent on repetitive administrative work so employees could focus more on customers,” he said.
While AI could help businesses analyse information and make recommendations, he said it did not remove the responsibility to exercise sound judgement, uphold integrity and consider the consequences of decisions affecting people’s lives.
“Technology may expand what we are capable of doing, but it is our values that must guide what we choose to do with that capability.
“We need to ensure smaller enterprises, workers and communities have meaningful opportunities to participate in and benefit from technological progress,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Oil ‘cocktail’ exports put Malaysia’s palm oil credentials under scrutiny, says maritime industry veteran
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The alleged blending of imported cooking oil with locally produced supplies before it is re-exported under a Malaysian label has raised concerns over product origin, traceability and food safety, with calls for the authorities to investigate the practice.
Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said the alleged practice, which industry players have described as an oil “cocktail”, warranted closer scrutiny from the authorities, particularly over product origin, quality and food safety.
The Edge
reported yesterday, citing industry sources, that imported palm oil was allegedly being blended with local supplies before being re-exported, potentially allowing foreign-origin oil to be marketed as Malaysian palm oil. Blending ratios of 75:25 or 80:20 were reportedly circulating in the market, the report said.
Jeyenderan said an examination of cargo manifests and bills of lading had raised concerns over how the oil’s country of origin was declared and how its actual composition was verified after blending.
Jeyenderan, who has more than 30 years of experience in the maritime industry, said independent laboratory tests were needed to establish whether the imported oil and the final blended product met the required quality and food safety standards.
He also questioned whether oil samples were tested before the vessels carrying the cargo left Malaysian waters, claiming the vessels concerned were not equipped with specialised laboratory facilities or qualified chemists to carry out detailed analyses.
“How could the actual composition and quality of the cargo be independently verified without proper laboratory testing?
“The issue is not just about blending different types of oil, but also about whether the origin and composition of the final product can be properly established before it is exported,” he said in a statement.
Jeyenderan said any possibility of contamination should be investigated through scientific testing rather than assumptions.
“If the oil is contaminated, what could be the impact on public health? Who is responsible for ensuring that the final product is safe for consumption?” he asked.
He said international rules already set clear expectations on origin, testing and traceability.
Under the Codex Alimentarius, the international food standards adopted by the United Nations’ Food and Agriculture Organization and World Health Organization, the General Standard for the Labelling of Prepackaged Foods requires a food’s country of origin to be declared if leaving it out would mislead or deceive consumers.
“Codex only allows the origin to shift when processing changes the nature of the food. Simply mixing imported oil with Malaysian oil does not change its nature, so declaring the blend as wholly Malaysian may mislead buyers,” he said.
On testing, he noted that international palm oil trade contracts under FOSFA International, including FOSFA Contract No. 81 issued jointly with the Palm Oil Refiners Association of Malaysia (PORAM), require independent analysis by qualified surveyors.
He also warned that Article 3 of the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), which applies to large operators from December 30, 2026, requires palm oil entering the EU to be traceable to the plots of land where it was produced.
“If foreign oil of unknown origin is mixed into Malaysian oil, the whole cargo may fail EUDR traceability. That puts genuine Malaysian exporters and our MSPO credibility at risk just as the regulation comes into force,” he said, referring to the Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil certification.
He urged the authorities to clarify the procedures governing the import, blending, sampling, quality certification and re-export of cooking oil, including which agencies are responsible for monitoring each stage.
He said proper documentation and independent laboratory testing were essential to ensure that products exported from Malaysia complied with the required standards and that their country of origin was accurately declared.
He added that failing to address the concerns could affect consumer confidence and Malaysia’s reputation as a food exporter.
An industry source said the alleged practice, if taking place, could displace locally produced palm oil in overseas markets and undermine confidence in Malaysia’s palm oil brand, including its MSPO certification and traceability framework.
“In the trade, this ‘cocktail’ is clearly an adulteration of Malaysian oil. It cannot be confirmed by the market alone, which is why the authorities need to check.
“Customs, MPOB (Malaysian Palm Oil Board) and Miti (Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry) already hold the import and origin records, so this can be checked quickly,” the source said.

Title: Zahid: 2,364 tahfiz students take up skills training, 900 secure Malaysian Skills Certification
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — A total of 2,364 tahfiz students enrolled in various skills training programmes at Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions between 2023 and 2025, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also the National TVET Council (MTVET) chairman, said data from the Department of Skills Development (JPK) under the Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma) also showed that 900 tahfiz students had obtained Malaysian Skills Certification under the National Occupational Skills Standard (NOSS).
In a written reply to Datuk Ahmad Saad @ Yahya (PN-Pokok Sena) posted on the Parliament website on the progress and challenges in implementing tahfiz TVET programmes, Ahmad Zahid said the NOSS certification comprised 609 students at Level 3, 285 at Level 4 and six at Level 5.
“In terms of expanding programmes under Kesuma the Manpower Department (JTM) increased the tahfiz TVET offerings from one institution in 2024 to four Advanced Technology Colleges (ADTEC), namely the campuses in Selandar, Kepala Batas, Kuala Lumpur and Jerantut,” he said.
He said the move had enabled 375 trainees to undergo full-time certificate-level training and micro-credential diploma programmes at the institutions as at Aug 31.
For initiatives under the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW), Ahmad Zahid, who is also its minister, said 1,165 tahfiz students had participated in TVET programmes ranging from short courses and modular training to degree-level programmes since the Professional Huffaz Programme was introduced at Universiti Kuala Lumpur (UniKL) in 2016.
He said the programme had since been expanded to TVETMARA, GIATMARA, the PERDA Institute of Advanced Skills (PERDA-TECH), Kolej KEDA and Kolej KETENGAH, with additional support through academic bridging programmes and mobile training units sent to tahfiz institutions in collaboration with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM).
Meanwhile, under the Ministry of Higher Education (MOHE), Ahmad Zahid said the programmes were implemented through the Techno-Huffaz Programme at polytechnics and the Lifelong Learning (PSH) approach at community colleges.
“As at October 2026, a total of 1,216 tahfiz students had participated in tahfiz TVET programmes at community colleges, comprising 1,196 students who attended 89 stand-alone micro-credential courses (MCSA) and 20 who took professional skills courses,” he said.
On implementation challenges, Ahmad Zahid said the main issues identified included differences in students’ academic qualifications and digital proficiency, the need to coordinate skills training schedules with Quran memorisation, and limited facilities and qualified instructors in rural areas.
He said the government would therefore continue to strengthen cooperation among ministries, agencies and industry players through flexible and modular courses.
“This is to ensure that the training remains relevant to current labour market needs and produces professional huffaz who are well-balanced in their religious knowledge, technical skills and employability,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Matrade warns businesses of scammers posing as agency officers to solicit upfront payments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) has alerted the business community and the public to fraudulent activities by individuals impersonating its personnel via email and WhatsApp.
Matrade said the perpetrators targeted vendors under the pretext of procuring urgent services for overseas trade delegations, booth translation services for international exhibitions, and corporate recreational events.
It said that under this guise, businesses were asked to provide sensitive documents, including company profiles, Companies Commission of Malaysia registration certificates, bank statements and Ministry of Finance certificates, which were subsequently used to fabricate fraudulent letters of award and government purchase orders.
“Matrade has received alarming reports that several companies have fallen victim to this syndicate and suffered financial losses by making upfront payments to third-party suppliers or designated ‘sub-orders’,” it said in a statement today.
Under this deceptive arrangement, scammers instruct awarded vendors to immediately purchase merchandise and gift supplies from an appointed sub-vendor to fulfil contract specifications before government disbursement, the agency said.
“These third-party entities are fraudulent shell accounts operated directly by the syndicate,” it said.
Matrade said it viewed the breach seriously and had lodged formal police reports, as well as filed complaints with CyberSecurity Malaysia and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission for digital forensic investigations and enforcement action.
To protect themselves, it advised businesses to verify all procurement requests and ensure communications originated from Matrade’s official corporate email addresses ending with “@matrade.gov.my”.
The agency said that its officers did not conduct procurement negotiations through commercial email providers such as Gmail and Yahoo or personal messaging platforms.
It also reminded businesses that all procurement exercises complied with the Malaysian Treasury Circulars (Pekeliling Perbendaharaan) and were conducted through formal, authorised government procurement channels.
“Matrade never requires vendors to deposit advances or settle external invoices with third-party sub-contractors,” it said.
It advised businesses not to disclose confidential financial or operational information without independent verification.
It urged companies that had transferred funds to fraudulent parties to contact the National Scam Response Centre at 997 immediately to help trace and freeze illicit banking transactions.
They should also lodge a police report at the nearest police station and provide transaction records, forged documents and chat transcripts to assist investigations, it said.
Matrade said it takes any form of fraud involving the agency’s name seriously and will take necessary action to protect the interests of exporters and the public.
For inquiries or to verify the authenticity of procurement requests claiming to originate from Matrade, businesses may contact the agency at 03-6207 7077 or email info@matrade.gov.my. — Bernama

Title: Armizan: Preliminary tests on 43 RON95 samples find no significant water contamination
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Preliminary laboratory tests on 43 petrol samples found water content below the minimum detection level, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said testing for water was given immediate priority, as a comprehensive analysis of all liquid properties and foreign contaminants would take more time.
“According to the preliminary report received from the Department of Chemistry dated October 29, 2026, all 43 samples analyzed recorded a water content of less than 0.05 per cent,” he said during Question Time.
“This figure falls well below the minimum threshold required for reporting, indicating no significant water contamination in the initial batch tested.”
The tests followed viral allegations that some petrol stations in Selangor and the northern states were selling contaminated RON95 that caused damage to cars. The claims first surfaced online last month and were later reported by the media.
Armizan said the remaining samples were still undergoing rigorous laboratory testing, and that a full report would be released to the public once the Department of Chemistry completes its analysis.
He said the first formal complaint was lodged with his ministry (KPDN) on October 3, prompting targeted inspections in Selangor and Perak. Perak received 25 complaints involving various petrol stations in the state throughout October.
As of October 31, inspections had covered eight petrol station brands across eight states, as well as three oil company depots.
A total of 262 RON95 samples were collected — 259 from petrol stations and three from oil company depots, Armizan told Parliament. — Bernama

Title: Rapid KL train congestion: Anthony Loke vows fix after PM’s directive
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 5 — The Transport Ministry is actively working to resolve train service congestion and overcome technical challenges faced by rail operators, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook.
“Rapid KL is working to address various technical challenges. We will resolve these technical issues to improve the service,” he said.
Loke told reporters this at his ministry’s get-together event with Tamil media practitioners at the Tropicana Golf and Country Resort here yesterday.
On Oct 30, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim directed the Transport Minister to swiftly resolve train congestion issues, expressing concern that they disrupt the public’s daily routine.
The directive followed a complaint posted by a user on the Threads platform to Anwar regarding overcrowding at train stations.
Meanwhile, Loke said train frequencies have been increased for the festive season to encourage more people to use public transport when returning to their hometowns.
He said Electric Train Service (ETS) trips from Kuala Lumpur to west coast states, including Kedah and Johor, received an encouraging response, with additional services scheduled ahead of Deepavali.
“We have added trips ahead of Deepavali, and Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is working to ensure service frequency is increased so that more people can take the train home,” he said.
Earlier, speaking on the event, Loke said it served as a platform to strengthen ties between the ministry and Tamil media practitioners in conjunction with Deepavali.
He noted that the media plays a vital role in disseminating information on ministry policies and services to all segments of society, including the Indian community.
Loke added that close cooperation with media practitioners is essential to ensure clear communication on road safety, public transport, the Road Transport Department (JPJ), and the aviation sector. — Bernama

Title: Heading east for Deepavali? Concessionaire releases travel time advisory for KLK and LPT1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Highway concessionaire AFA Prime Berhad has activated its Travel Time Advisory for the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Highway (KLK) and the East Coast Expressway Phase 1 (LPT1) ahead of an anticipated holiday traffic surge for Deepavali.
The staggered travel schedule aims to ease bottlenecks across the arterial eastern corridor, particularly at the high-volume Gombak, Bentong, and Jabor toll plazas that link the Klang Valley to Pahang, Terengganu, and Kelantan.
Under its “Smart Travel” roadmap, the operator has segmented recommended departure windows by state destination to distribute traffic evenly across peak holiday dates.
For outbound journeys from Kuala Lumpur and Selangor on Saturday, Nov 7, motorists passing through the Gombak Toll Plaza are advised to stagger their departures according to their destination.
Travellers heading to Kelantan are advised to start earliest, between 6am and 9am or from 5pm to 8pm.
Motorists bound for Terengganu should depart between 9am and 12pm or from 8pm to 11pm, while those heading to Pahang are urged to enter the expressway between 12pm and 4pm or during the secondary 8pm to 11pm window.
For the return commute towards the Klang Valley on Monday, Nov 9, drivers originating from Pahang are encouraged to use any toll plaza between 7am and 10am or from 7pm to 11pm.
Motorists returning from Terengganu through the Jabor Toll Plaza should target travel between 10am and 1pm or from 8pm to 10pm.
Meanwhile, traffic heading back from Kelantan via the Bentong Toll Plaza is advised to move between 4pm and 8pm or during the late 9pm to midnight slot.
To maximise efficiency, motorists are also encouraged to take advantage of “Free Travel Hours” during the midnight to 6am off-peak window on both designated dates.
Private car owners are specifically cautioned to avoid heavy express bus departure surges at the Gombak Toll Plaza, which peak between 9.30am and 12 noon as well as between 9.30pm and midnight.
AFA Prime managing director and chief executive officer Ahmad Faizi Latifi Ahmad Faiz reminded motorists to navigate cautiously through ongoing construction zones along the KLK, where active widening works are currently underway as part of the RM2.1 billion KLK Expansion project.
“We urge all road users to comply with the traffic instructions and signage at work zones, to reduce speed and to drive with extra care,” he said, adding that dedicated emergency response teams and patrol units will be deployed at strategic points along both expressways to provide rapid assistance.

Title: Anwar heads to Melaka to drum up Pakatan momentum ahead of Nov 14 polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to attend five programmes in Melaka tomorrow, including participating in Pakatan Harapan (PH) campaign activities in conjunction with the Melaka State Election.
Anwar said two of the programmes he would be attending are the 2026 Prime Minister’s Golden Hand Award (MATEPM) ceremony and the Melaka State Madani Aspirations Tour.
“Insya-Allah, I will be in Melaka tomorrow for several engagements in this historic state. I will first visit Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) to meet educators and students at an official event, before heading to several other locations to boost the Harapan momentum in Melaka,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Based on the schedule shared in the post, Anwar is slated to begin his visit by attending the MATEPM 2026 at Dewan Canselor, UTeM, at 2.30 pm, before joining the Melaka State Madani Aspirations Tour for the Klebang state constituency in Taman Bukit Rambai at 4.45 pm.
In the evening, the PH chairman is scheduled to attend the ‘Malam Harapan’ programme at Dewan Pay Fong, SJK Pay Fong, at 7.30 pm, followed by the ‘Malam Ramah Mesra Melaka Rumah Kita Bersama PMX’ programme for the Paya Rumput constituency at Taman Seri Karanjong, Paya Rumput, at 8.30 pm.
Anwar is scheduled to conclude his visit by attending the ‘Sinar Deepavali Harapan’ celebration at Dewan Japerun Peringgit, Peringgit, at 9.30 pm.
Polling is on Nov 14, with early voting set for Nov 10. — Bernama

Title: Deepavali toll relief: 50pc discount on major highways this Friday and Saturday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Motorists travelling across the country for the Deepavali celebrations will enjoy a 50 per cent toll discount on Friday and Saturday, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi announced today.
The festive waiver takes effect from 12.00am on Friday and concludes at 11.59pm on Saturday. Putrajaya estimates the two-day toll concession will require approximately RM20.11 million in federal compensation payouts to highway concessionaires, subject to post-holiday traffic volume verifications.
The discount applies to private Class 1 passenger vehicles across all interstate expressways, alongside Class 2 commercial vehicles crossing the Penang Bridge.
However, standard toll charges remain in force at the country’s two southern international border crossings: the Bangunan Sultan Iskandar (BSI) toll plaza on the North-South Expressway and the Tanjung Kupang toll plaza along the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link (Linkedua).
“This decision reflects the MADANI Government’s continued concern and commitment to safeguarding the welfare and well-being of the people, regardless of race, religion or belief, while strengthening the spirit of unity and harmony within Malaysia’s multiracial society.
“This initiative is expected to help ease the people’s travel expenses, particularly for members of the Hindu community who return to their hometowns or visit family members to celebrate Deepavali, thereby giving greater meaning to the festive spirit through family ties and togetherness,” the minister said.
The Works Ministry, through the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), will supervise operational coordination with all highway concessionaires to guarantee smooth implementation across automated lanes.
The ministry urged long-distance drivers to plan their travel times carefully to avoid peak bottleneck hours, maintain adequate credit balances in their Touch ‘n Go cards and RFID e-wallets, and track live traffic updates through LLM’s official monitoring channels.
Extending festive greetings to the Hindu community, the ministry expressed hope that the celebrations would foster warmth, harmony, and mutual respect across Malaysia’s multiracial society, while wishing all holidaymakers safe journeys to their hometowns.

Title: Seven foreigners held, RM1.08m in drugs seized in Bukit Mertajam raids
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 5 — Police arrested seven foreigners and seized suspected methylenedioxy methamphetamine (MDMA) powder and ketamine worth RM1.08 million during raids on two premises in Bukit Tengah here on Nov 1.
Seberang Perai Tengah (SPT) district police chief ACP Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said a team from the district Narcotics Crime Investigation Division raided the premises at 12.50 am following surveillance and intelligence gathering.
“Police arrested six men and a woman, all aged between 25 and 38. Inspections of both premises uncovered MDMA powder and ketamine valued at an estimated RM1.08 million,” he said in a statement tonight.
Nik Aminuddin said urine screening tests revealed that two of the suspects tested positive for methamphetamine, while the other five tested negative. None of the suspects had prior criminal or drug-related records.
All suspects have been remanded for seven days from Nov 1 to 7 to assist in investigations under Section 39B, Section 12(3), and Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Police are continuing investigations to track down the drug syndicate’s distribution network. — Bernama

Title: Penang ferry free for Malaysians on Nov 8 for Deepavali
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 5 — The Penang Port Commission (PPC) and Penang Port Sdn Bhd (PPSB) will offer free ferry rides to Malaysian citizens on Nov 8 in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration.
PPC chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said the free ferry rides would be available to passengers departing from both Pangkalan Sultan Abdul Halim (PSAH) in Butterworth and Pangkalan Raja Tun Uda (PRTU) in George Town.
“The free ferry service will operate according to the latest timetable. The public is advised to plan their journeys in advance and refer to the official websites and social media channels of PPC and PPSB for the latest ferry timetable,” he said in a statement.
Yeoh said the initiative reflected the continued commitment of PPC and PPSB to facilitating public travel, particularly during festive seasons, while helping to ease traffic congestion in Penang.
Citing figures from last year’s Deepavali celebration, Yeoh said 7,780 foot passengers and 1,518 two-wheeled vehicles used the ferry service in both directions.
He said the Penang ferry service also recorded a 5.61 per cent increase in passenger numbers from January to September this year compared with the corresponding period last year. — Bernama
